content: Uroquid-Acid No. 2, also known as Utac, is a combination medication containing methenamine and sodium acid phosphate. Below is a detailed explanation of its dosing, indications, interactions, adverse effects, and pharmacokinetics: Dosing: Initial Dose: Two tablets taken orally every six hours, accompanied by liberal fluid intake. Maintenance Dose: One to two tablets taken orally every 12 hours. This medication should only be used after a urinary tract infection (UTI) has been eradicated with appropriate antibiotics. Indications: Methenamine: Used for the prophylaxis and suppression of chronic, recurrent UTIs when long-term therapy is required. Sodium Acid Phosphate: Functions as a urinary acidifier. Safety and Efficacy: The safety and efficacy of this combination have not been fully established. Sodium acid phosphate and sodium phosphate rectal preparations are contraindicated due to the risk of pharmacodynamic synergism, which can increase toxicity and cause electrolyte disturbances or hypovolemia. Drug Interactions: 1. Baloxavir Marboxil: Sodium acid phosphate reduces the absorption of baloxavir marboxil in the gastrointestinal tract due to cation binding. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 2. Tetracyclines (e.g., omadacycline, sarecycline): Sodium acid phosphate impairs the absorption of tetracyclines, reducing their efficacy. Separate dosing or modify therapy as needed. 3. Amphetamines (e.g., dextroamphetamine, lisdexamfetamine, methamphetamine): Sodium acid phosphate increases renal clearance of amphetamines, reducing their plasma levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 4. Deflazacort: Co-administration with sodium acid phosphate can decrease serum potassium levels. Monitor potassium levels closely. 5. Multivalent Cations (e.g., calcium, aluminum, iron): These can bind to sodium acid phosphate, reducing drug absorption. Avoid concurrent use or monitor closely. Adverse Effects: Common side effects include dysuria, gastric upset, nausea, rash, diarrhea, stomach pain, and vomiting. Pregnancy and Lactation: Pregnancy Category C: Methenamine is generally considered acceptable, but caution is advised as the risk to the fetus cannot be ruled out. Lactation: Methenamine is excreted in human milk. Use caution as the risk to the infant is uncertain. Pharmacokinetics: Half-Life: 3-6 hours. Absorption: Well absorbed; 10-30% is hydrolyzed by gastric acid unless the tablet is enteric-coated. Peak Urine Time: 2 hours for hippurate salt and 3-8 hours for mandelate salt. Metabolism: Partially metabolized by the liver (10-25%). Excretion: Primarily excreted in the urine (90%). Onset of Action: 1-3 hours. Duration of Action: 1-3 hours. Bioavailability: Approximately 66%. Mechanism of Action: Methenamine: In acidic urine, methenamine is hydrolyzed into ammonia and formaldehyde, which act as bactericidal agents. It does not convert to formaldehyde in the serum. Sodium Acid Phosphate: Acts as a urinary acidifier and exerts an osmotic effect in the gastrointestinal tract. Additional Notes: Sodium acid phosphate and potassium phosphates administered intravenously can increase serum potassium levels. Avoid or use alternative drugs in such cases. For tetracyclines, separate dosing from sodium acid phosphate-containing products to avoid reduced efficacy. This information is provided for general educational purposes. Always consult a healthcare provider or pharmacist for the most current and personalized guidance regarding medication use.
